plan: My value is $30. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. If I bid less, I risk losing the item even when winning would be profitable. If I bid more, I might pay more than the item is worth to me. The worst-case scenario is paying close to my value, but still having a potential profit margin. I'll bid my true value of $30 to maximize my expected profit.

My private value is $35. To maximize profit, I want to win only if my bid leaves me with positive earnings. Since the second-highest bid determines my payment, I'll bid strategically just above my expected competing bids. Given the $0-$49 range, I'll bid around $36-$37 to create a buffer. This allows me to potentially win while ensuring I don't overpay relative to my true value.

My private value is $6. In a first-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy depends on predicting others' behavior. Since the value is randomly drawn, I'll bid strategically near my value. Bidding my full $6 risks losing money if others bid lower. I'll bid slightly above my value at $6.5 to increase winning chances while minimizing overpayment risk. This balanced approach protects potential profit margin.
